_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_onboard_missing_required_positional_defect.md (PR #75, 2026-06-07, Gradient MSP billing sync).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (SecretEnv GRADIENT_TOKEN, GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY, GRADIENT_PARTNER_API_KEY and GRADIENT_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; Files = the config the run really uses first, an explicit --config or GRADIENT_CONFIG winning, then the 0600 credential store and the legacy config; every other config, store and profiles.json any --config or --home could mean is held with cliutil.HoldFile; ConfigFields and StoredRecords auth_header, token, access_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret; StdinFlags --stdin, a JSON body put on one line first and feedback's prose body taken off stdin and handed back after Start (compactStdinBody, RestoreFeedbackStdin); CredentialHeaders GRADIENT-TOKEN; BaseURL GRADIENT_BASE_URL, default https://app.usegradient.com/api; Origins the base URL only, Gradient having no token host; no ResponseFields or URLEnv, because the Synthesize API answers no credential and no token URL is read). credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them. Every sink is routed: stdout and stderr at the descriptor; the API client (client.OutboundGuard), feedback, deliver and the probe through credkit.Transport; cache, journal, teach log, learnings audit, profile, platform profile, rate-limit lock, download, export and the pushes.jsonl and alerts.jsonl ledgers through credkit.WriteFile, AppendFile, OpenFile and NewWriter; SQLite through internal/credsql (credkit.SQLDriver, the MCP sql value cap set as each connection opens); the MCP server through MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP; the MCP server's CLI child through RunCommand; terminal checks through credkit.Terminal; auth set-token holds the token it reads from stdin; the composed GRADIENT-TOKEN is held where it is derived (composed-auth-key-pair). The 0600 credential store and config.toml are credential sources: their writes are a declared exemption, outside the kit in cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, and both are in Files.
handfixes.why: Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, derived-credential-parts-held, output-units-reassembled, ledger-files-withheld: replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). The connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, scattered/encodings/outbound/secrets matchers, store withholding driver, MCP output wrappers and body, URL and TOML-string readers kept growing per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time; the kit is one shared implementation of the leak contract, checked byte for byte against tools/maintainer/credkit (vendor_credkit.py --check). It closes the print's open Codex class credential-split-across-output-members, encoded variant: every 8-character piece of a held value is found after percent-decoding at every depth, so feedback text carrying GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY's two halves, each triple percent-encoded in its own member, prints neither and writes neither to feedback.jsonl. internal/credwire/open_classes_test.go TestFeedbackEncodedHalvesWithheld runs the built binary with that input and an unheld control that must reach stdout and feedback.jsonl; seen failing on the pre-kit tree (115873121, .review/seen/prewire-open-classes.log) and passing after. The short decoded Basic password printed in another response member (TestDecodedBasicPasswordElsewhereInResponse) is P2 for Gradient, whose documented responses carry no authorization member, and is not held by the kit: kept skipped and recorded as a kit item.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and the kit-wrapped SQLite driver.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The GRADIENT_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds (a profile, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl, the learn tables) is withheld by the shared credential kit at the sink (credkit-wiring). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path, holds through the kit in its held pass, and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes. Seen failing on the pre-kit tree (115873121, .review/seen/prewire-journal.log: the raw session key, argv after --, the typed flag kept and failed flags not opaque) and passing after; the shape and tests follow rocketcyber's entry of the same id. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains (credkit-wiring), so every credential in config.toml is held before the program can print a byte, a config that does not parse included: the kit reads the whole file, and where a declared credential key, headers, auth_header or base_url is followed by a separator it holds the value after it. A credential in a malformed config.toml (an unquoted bare value, a valid line then a broken table, a credential after 64 KiB of padding, inside auth_header, inside [headers]) or in a base_url that does not parse never appears in gradient-cli startup output (stdout and stderr, plain and --json; doctor and vendor get) or in gradient-mcp's stderr and JSON-RPC responses, for the discovered default config and an explicit one (--config, GRADIENT_CONFIG for the MCP server). A run the kit refuses to start (exit 78) prints no credential either.
handfixes.why: Fleet rule (Startup ordering): the holder must be installed before config is loaded or any startup diagnostic can print, in both the CLI and the MCP server, and a config that fails to parse still has every value in it held. internal/credwire/startup_test.go TestStartupConfigHeldFirst builds and runs both binaries (.exe on Windows) under GRADIENT_HOME in a sandbox. Proved both ways: with credkit.Start removed from both mains the base_url case fails (the URL parse error prints its password; .review/seen/mutant-startup-no-kit.log), and it passes with the kit. The TOML parser's own errors name no value, so the five malformed-file cases pass with or without a holder; they stay as the contract's named inputs.

handfixes.summary: Doc examples/Command-Reference rows keep their REQUIRED positional (billing <serviceId>, services get <serviceId>, mappings update <serviceId>, accounts update-one <accountId>); the press dropped them for some commands
handfixes.why: The press inconsistently annotates required positionals: in the SAME Command Reference it wrote `billing <serviceId>` for some commands but dropped the positional for siblings (accounts update-one, mappings update, services get) even though all require one (Usage: ... <foo> [flags]). check_cli_claims is blind (it parses the first bareword as the subcommand and ignores trailing positionals), so a non-runnable example sails through every mechanical gate - only iterated adversarial review caught it. A reprint reverts the examples to the no-positional form (e.g. `gradient-cli billing --account-id ...` which errors 'serviceId is required', exit 2).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press doc generator: emit required positionals consistently in every Command-Reference row + runnable example. Tracked in project_onboard_missing_required_positional_defect.

handfixes.summary: Governance Write tier hand-promoted to include the 5 verb-less writes (usage push, billing, alert send, alerting, import) the keyword classifier missed; 14 total
handfixes.why: gen_governance keyed on write-verb keywords, so the 5 verb-less / non-standard-verb POSTs (usage push, billing, alert send, alerting, import) fell to the Read tier. Hand-authored governance.md Write tier names all 14 mutations (union, not replace). A reprint regenerates governance.md from the blind classifier and silently demotes the 5 to Read.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Real fix is a method-aware gen_governance (classify from pp:method). Tracked in project_gen_governance_misses_verbless_writes / project_governance_rewrite_union_not_replace.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For gradient the manifest gained: GRADIENT_BASE_URL, GRADIENT_PARTNER_API_KEY, GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY. server.json gained: GRADIENT_BASE_URL, GRADIENT_PARTNER_API_KEY, GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: GRADIENT_BASE_URL, GRADIENT_PARTNER_API_KEY, GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP mirror refuses `usage push --file`, which names a file on the machine that runs the MCP server: the command declares the flag in its mcp:read-flags annotation, so press 4.34 leaves it out of the tool schema and refuses it
handfixes.why: `usage push --file` names a counts file the CLI reads off the local disk. The MCP server runs this CLI as the account that hosts it and forwarded the flag, so one tool call could point the read at any file that account can reach and get the parsed rows back. Reproduced on origin/main d3cbf7129 (connector tree unchanged at 518e1edff) with the real MCP binary and a recording stand-in for the companion CLI: tools/call with the flag set reached the CLI argv. The flag's usage text did not say it took a path, so isFilesystemPathFlag missed it and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath stayed green; the usage text now says 'Path to', which makes that test fail until the floor names the flag, so a reprint that drops this entry fails the build. The operator still passes the flag on the command line. Found while vetting the gosec G304 finding its `#nosec G304` annotation hid from the security gate. gradient 4.34.2 reprint: press 4.34 replaced the hand-listed blockedDestinationFlags with a per-command blocked set built from mcp:read-flags / mcp:write-flags annotations; the novel now declares --file there (check_mcp_file_flags.py failed on the fresh tree until it did: the value reached the companion CLI).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: classify a novel command's local-input flags as filesystem flags from the flag's type or a declared annotation, not only from phrases in its usage text.

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: raw Gradient bodies never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Gradient's docs say responses are never cached, and a raw Gradient body (client and vendor records) has no business in cache files. c.NoCache = true in the guard's client hook (gradient_guard.go). The shared credential kit (credkit-wiring) would withhold a cache file carrying a held credential, but it does not stop ordinary response data being cached, so this stays.

The confirm gate stays installed so a mirrored command a later print adds that is neither read-only nor local previews and sends only with confirm: true.
handfixes.why: Work order: an MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/gradient_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools after RegisterAll. TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm fails on any registered tool that is not read-only, not on its local list and has no confirm gate; TestMCPSendsOnlyReads (black-box) checks a full MCP battery sends only GETs and the two logins. handfixes.why: The generated docs describe the press defaults (a response cache) that the credential layer turns off; a reprint restores the false promise and drops the transcripts reasoning the work order requires. handfixes.summary: A client built under --dry-run refuses every request at its transport, so no write, mint or refresh can reach Gradient whatever a command does with the client; `auth login --dry-run` sends nothing too.
handfixes.why: Defense in depth beside dry-run-never-mints: the generated preview path returns before sending, and this transport makes a missed branch fail closed. The black-box test runs writes and auth login under --dry-run from a cold start against a fake token host and API host and counts zero requests on both. Not a credential check, so the shared credential kit does not replace it: the dry-run transport sits inside the origin pin and outside the kit's Transport (gradient_guard.go).

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (create or update a company or contact, delete a contact, create an order, update or cancel a subscription) returns a preview of the request and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true; the gate wraps every non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so one a later print adds is gated too.
handfixes.why: Work order connector note: every MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. Press 4.34.2's in-process endpoint handlers (makeAPIHandler) send writes directly. The gate (hand file internal/mcp/gradient_endpoint_confirm.go) is installed by one anchored line in the generated tools.go after every registration and before the read-only drop. The black-box test drives the real MCP server against a fake Gradient: no write without confirm, the string "true" previews, and boolean true sends (control). Ported to gradient from the pax8 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: config.toml keeps base_url without its userinfo and query: save() (auth set-token, a saved token) and the legacy-config scrub pass it through baseURLWithoutCredentials (internal/config/gradient_persist.go), so a password or query value that GRADIENT_BASE_URL or the file carries is not written to config.toml. A base URL that does not parse and could hide either is replaced by the built-in default; an unresolved {placeholder} host is kept as written.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 4.34.2 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: the generated save persists base_url as configured, environment value included (`GRADIENT_BASE_URL='https://app.usegradient.com/api?api_key=X' auth set-token` wrote X into config.toml). config.toml is a credential source written outside the shared credential kit (a declared exemption, credkit-wiring), so the kit cannot withhold it there; this is the one part of the old persistence filter the kit does not duplicate, rewritten on the standard library as rocketcyber did (the old filter's credential-name recognizers, held-value refusal and token_url handling are retired with the layer; Gradient has no token URL). TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential (black-box, auth set-token on the built binary) and TestBaseURLWithoutCredentials (unit) prove it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated save should persist base_url without its userinfo and query.

handfixes.summary: The GRADIENT-TOKEN header and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the API base URL; every redirect hop must stay on that origin, a non-ASCII host never matches, and an unparseable base URL pins nothing (every request refused). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/gradient_guard.go) outside the shared credential kit's Transport (client.OutboundGuard), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send.
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the credential header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the primary Authorization header, so GRADIENT-TOKEN followed a redirect to another host. One origin (Gradient has no token host), checked at the transport (outermost) and in CheckRedirect before the generated check can resolve an off-origin name in DNS. Kept beside the shared credential kit (credkit-wiring): the kit's Transport refuses a request only when it carries a held credential to an origin Declarations.Origins does not allow, while the pin refuses every request and redirect off the API origin and every request when the base URL does not parse, credential or not. The kit does not do the same job, so the pin is not retired.

handfixes.summary: GRADIENT_VENDOR_API_KEY + GRADIENT_PARTNER_API_KEY derive the GRADIENT-TOKEN header (base64 "vendor:partner") when GRADIENT_TOKEN is unset; the derived value is an env override (never written to config.toml), counts as an environment credential for the untrusted-config refusal, ignores an unresolved .mcpb ${user_config.*} placeholder, and is held through the shared credential kit the moment it is derived (cliutil.Hold, credkit.Hold); both keys are held from startup (Declarations.SecretEnv).
handfixes.why: Synthesize issues a Vendor and a Partner API key and authenticates base64("<vendor>:<partner>") in the GRADIENT-TOKEN header (the official SDK's BuildGradientToken). Press 4.34.2 knows only GRADIENT_TOKEN; without these edits in the generated config.go an operator who exports the key pair as Gradient hands it out gets no credential at all. The 4.24 hand edit read the keys with os.Getenv, so an MCP host that leaves the bundle placeholder in place would send the literal "${user_config.gradient_vendor_api_key}" as a key; EnvOverride drops it. markEnvOverride keeps the derived token out of config.toml (only credentials.toml holds a credential). The connector's own derived-parts holder (FunnelHold of vendor, partner, raw and token) is retired: the kit's decoders read the base64 header, the pair and its halves (credkit-wiring).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Composed auth (two env vars combined into one header by a template) is not expressible in the press spec; a press feature would be x-auth-compose: {header, format: base64("{a}:{b}"), env: [A, B]}.

handfixes.summary: doctorShippedBaseURL is empty: https://app.usegradient.com/api is Gradient's one real API root, so doctor dials it and probes the credential instead of reporting 'base_url is still the shipped placeholder' on every healthy install
handfixes.why: The fleet doctor-verdict template set doctorShippedBaseURL to the connector's default base URL; for a single-endpoint vendor that default is the real API (press-traps s5: 42 connectors on 2026-10-24), so doctor printed ERROR on every correctly configured install and never probed the credential. The replay restores doctor_verdict.go from the shipped tree only when the reprint lacks it, so this edit survives; a re-mint of the doctor template would restore the real host.

handfixes.summary: The .mcpb bundle asks for GRADIENT_TOKEN or the vendor + partner key pair, all three optional, with descriptions that say which wins
handfixes.why: The published bundle marked all three credentials required. GRADIENT_TOKEN wins over the pair, so an operator holding only the pair (as Synthesize issues it) had to type something into the token field, which then shadowed the working pair and every call returned 401. The CLI ignores an unresolved ${user_config.*} placeholder, so an empty optional field is safe. server.json and mcp-install.md (msp-skills layer) should say the same at onboard.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err. The rows are buffered and written once through the shared credential kit (credkit.WriteFile, credkit-wiring).
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing.

handfixes.summary: usage push refuses a unitCount that is negative, NaN or infinite (CSV NaN/+Inf parse as floats), at validation, before any row is sent
handfixes.why: Codex r1 P2 (one-line fix): NaN and +Inf passed the negative-only check, so --dry-run accepted the file and a real push sent the preceding rows before JSON encoding refused the bad count, leaving a partial push.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO); ChatGPT on the web needs the operator's own HTTPS host with the MCP HTTP token (press 4.34.2 HTTP mode), and no page says HTTP mode is paused.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).
